titre: Getting or updating a family record book (livret de famille): duplicate, second book
resume: First book at birth, update after a recognition or a divorce, second book when you are separated or have lost it: where to go, which documents to bring, and it is free.
aQuoiCaSert: The family record book (livret de famille) brings together extracts of the civil registry records of the parents and their children. You are often asked for it: enrolling at school or a crèche, Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office) file, legal aid (aide juridictionnelle), opening an account for the child. After a separation, the parent who no longer has the original book can get their own, free of charge.
quiEstConcerne: Parents, married or not, when their first child is born.
A separated or divorced parent who does not have the original book.
Holders of a book that has been lost, stolen or damaged, or that needs updating.
aSavoir: Birth of a first child: the book is issued free of charge by the town hall (mairie) of the place of birth, on presentation of an ID document. The other parent only appears in it if they appear on the child's birth certificate, hence the importance of recognition (reconnaissance) for unmarried parents.

Second book after separation or divorce: it can be requested at any time, free of charge, from the town hall where you live. Married parents: bring proof of the divorce or legal separation. Parents in a PACS (civil partnership) or living together: explain why you need your own book and attach supporting evidence.

Loss or theft: the second book is rebuilt from civil registry records and is marked "second livret". Damaged book: a duplicate is issued. Issue is free, but a town hall may charge for duplicates from the second one.
Updates: birth, recognition, marriage, divorce, change of surname or first name must be entered in the book, free of charge, usually at the town hall where the event was registered.
Using a falsified or out-of-date book can be punished by a fine of up to €1,500 (€3,000 for a repeat offense).
Time to obtain it: usually a few weeks, while the town hall receives the records from the other towns concerned. Plan ahead if you need it for a procedure.

documents.libelle: ID document of the applying parent (original)
documents.detail: Valid ID card, passport or residence permit. Also required when collecting the book.

documents.libelle: Proof of address less than 3 months old
documents.detail: Requested in case of loss, theft or damage.
Married parents: divorce decision or approved agreement. PACS or living together: proof of separate addresses, statements.

documents.libelle: Information on the records to be entered
documents.detail: Surnames, first names, dates and places of birth of the parents and children, date and place of marriage.

documents.libelle: Sworn statement of loss or theft, or the damaged book
documents.detail: In case of theft, reporting it to the police or gendarmerie is recommended.

documents.libelle: Record or decision to be entered (update)
documents.detail: Birth certificate, recognition certificate, divorce judgment, change of name decision, depending on the event.

documents.libelle: Family record book (scanned copy of every page)
documents.detail: A full copy is enough for many procedures.

etapes.detail: First book, update after an event, second book after a separation, or replacement after loss, theft or damage.

Second book or replacement: the town hall where you live. Update: usually the town hall where the event was registered. Event that took place abroad: the Service central d'état civil (the central civil registry office) in Nantes, by post.
Original ID document, proof of address less than 3 months old, proof of divorce or separation, information on all the records, old book if damaged. Call the town hall for opening hours.

etapes.titre: Submit the request at the town hall

etapes.detail: At the town hall where you applied, with your ID document, usually after a few weeks.
Every page, so you can provide a copy without having to travel.
